summary: solidity-map ships heavily obfuscated payload under pino cover story
details: Package published as 'solidity-map' with a description about vulnerability management ships code copied from the pino logging library (lib/levels.js, lib/proto.js, lib/tools.js, lib/transport.js, lib/worker.js are upstream pino sources; index.js exports middleware labeled 'pino'; keywords are ['fast','logger','stream','json']). The author 'Robert King <hello@jsonspack.com>' is unrelated to pino's maintainers, and the published name does not correspond to the shipped functionality. Alongside this cover-story mismatch, lib/config.js is a ~4.3MB single-line IIFE heavily obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style transforms: a 26,185-element rotating string array, two decoder functions (Y/k), hex-escaped object keys, control-flow flattening, and ~44,484 inlined decoded-string operations. Legitimate pino contains no such file. The combination of a trojaned cover identity (pino clone republished under an unrelated package name by an unrelated author) with a large obfuscated module that executes when the package is loaded is the structural shape of a supply-chain trojan whose runtime behavior is deliberately hidden from static review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
